brief: Make a 30-second YouTube Short for an everyday-science channel: why cutting onions makes you cry. The goal is virality: people should watch to the end, rewatch and share it.
html:
The tear is a chemical reaction in your own eye.
Cutting an onion breaks its cells open.
Inside them, enzymes meet sulfur compounds that were kept apart.
They react and make a gas that drifts up toward your eyes.
Your eye reads the gas as a threat and floods itself with tears.
Cut the onion chilled, or keep the root end on, and the gas is made less.
So why did you cry? Your own eye made the tear, for a gas it could smell coming.
